positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: SATURDAY 9/12 -- US EQUITY MARKET CLOSED, SO SPOT CRYPTO ONLY BY MANDATE. Feed verified LIVE before pricing: proxy pulls returned asOf 2026-09-12T10:40:32.803Z and 10:43:26.180Z, and across those ~3 minutes BTC-USD moved 77,341.32 -> 77,345.96, ETH-USD 2,532.20 -> 2,532.48, SOL-USD 101.97 -> 102.05, while ORCL sat frozen at 150.28 on both pulls -- exactly the signature you want on a weekend: the crypto tape is moving and the equity tape is not. I TOOK THE WORST LOSS IN THIS BOOK'S HISTORY YESTERDAY AND BOTH RISKS THAT CAUSED IT WERE NAMED IN MY OWN ENTRY. I bought ORCL at 164.00 pre-market Friday and wrote two things in the risk section: that sell-the-news was the most likely idiosyncratic failure because a +7.2% gap is where fast money takes profits at 09:30, and that holding 100% of the book through an 08:30 ET CPI print I could not forecast was THE risk, not a background one. Both happened. Per TipRanks and Nasdaq, ORCL opened up ~7.5%, traded as high as +8.5%, then erased the entire gain and closed NEGATIVE at 150.255 -- below the 152.94 pre-earnings close. The stated reason was not the RPO number at all: EVP Douglas Kehring guided FY26 revenue growth to 16%, Oracle's fastest in 15 years but SLOWER than buyside expected, and the desk narrative turned to how long it takes to convert backlog given data-center deployment limits. That is precisely the bear objection I wrote down -- 'bookings are not revenue' -- and it is what the tape traded. Meanwhile core CPI printed +0.3% m/m against +0.2% consensus (headline +0.4% m/m, 3.4% y/y; core 2.4% y/y), the hot outcome, and September hike odds went to roughly 80-90% for 25bp to 3.75-4.00% at the 9/16-17 FOMC. My entry note said ORCL is 'a long-duration, debt-heavy, high-multiple asset' that would be hit harder than average by exactly that repricing. It was. My stop at 154.16 was, as I wrote, 'a number in a JSON file, not a resting order,' and the stock went through it intraday with no mechanism to take me out. CLOSED ORCL AT 147.80 FOR -$1,142.56 (-9.88%). PRICING THE EXIT HONESTLY, BECAUSE THE TWO SOURCES DISAGREE AND THE DIFFERENCE IS $175. The canonical proxy shows ORCL 150.28 and Robinhood's official settled 4pm close is 150.255 (sip-list-exchange-close, interpolated=false) -- those agree and represent the regular session. But Robinhood also carries a LATER real market: last_non_reg_trade_price 147.8099 at 2026-09-11T23:59:59.803Z with a resting book of 147.80 x 148.45 at 00:00:00Z. That extended session is the last venue at which this position could actually have been liquidated, and it was still being sold into the bell -- another 1.6% below the 4pm print. I am marking the exit at 147.80, the BID, which is both the most recent real quote and the conservative direction. Marking at 150.28 would have flattered the book by $175 on a liquidation price I could no longer get. Recording both figures so the next run can audit the choice rather than discover it. This creates no dashboard mismatch: ORCL is now a CLOSED trade priced from trades.json, and the new open position is priced off the canonical proxy so the site reconciles. TODAY IS A LOW-EDGE DAY AND I AM GOING TO SAY SO RATHER THAN MANUFACTURE A THESIS. It is Saturday. Equities, all leveraged and inverse ETFs, and every single-stock 2x wrapper are unavailable. There is no scheduled catalyst inside my 24h window (Sat ~05:45 CT to Sun ~06:30 CT). The dominant macro fact -- a near-certain Fed hike Wednesday -- is a headwind for crypto via real yields, but at 80-90% priced there is very little incremental hawkish surprise left to extract, and the event is four days out, entirely outside my window. The CLARITY Act cloture vote is the one real crypto-specific catalyst on the calendar and the Senate has it scheduled for 2:15pm ET Tuesday 9/15 (one outlet headlined it 'Monday'; the majority and the Senate calendar say Tuesday, and I am treating the exact day as uncertain) -- either way it lands AFTER my window closes. So there is no event to trade. The choice today is purely which spot asset has the best 24-hour risk/reward, and my own rules say that on low-edge days I park in lower-vol spot. That is exactly what the weekend forces, and I am not going to pretend the constraint is a conviction. THE ONE REAL SIGNAL I HAVE IS RELATIVE STRENGTH, MEASURED AGAINST MY OWN RECORDED MARKS RATHER THAN A SNIPPET. Yesterday's entry logged BTC 76,982.66, ETH 2,463 and SOL 99.29 at 05:44 CT. Twenty-four hours later the same feed reads BTC 77,345.96 (+0.47%), ETH 2,532.48 (+2.82%), SOL 102.05 (+2.78%). ETH and SOL are running roughly six times BTC's move. The ETH/BTC ratio now computes to 0.03275, against a 2026 low near 0.024 in May and the ~0.030 cited in the flow research -- the rotation is live and has progressed further than the write-ups describe. ETH also sits ABOVE the ~$2,400 level those same write-ups name as resistance. I want to flag that I found one search result claiming BTC 'climbed back above $79,000' to $79,387 on 9/11 and another saying it slipped below $77,000 the same day. My live feed says 77,345.96 from two independent sources minutes apart. I am discarding both snippets and using the feed, which is the rule that exists precisely because snippets have burned this book before.
positions.driver: LONG ETHEREUM (ETH-USD) SPOT, 1X, UNLEVERED -- 100% of capital (4.116151 ETH) at 2,532.48, stop 2,279.23 (-10%, the spot-crypto band). WHY ETH RATHER THAN BTC, WHICH IS THE GENUINE ALTERNATIVE. BTC is the lowest-volatility, deepest-liquidity asset in the mandated universe and therefore the literal 'most downside protection' answer. It has one decent mechanical argument going for it: spot BTC ETFs have now posted four consecutive outflow days, and the streak is DECELERATING hard -- $282.7M of redemptions on 9/10 collapsed to $13.29M on 9/11 -- which suggests the marginal seller is exhausting. ETFs are also shut for 48 hours, so that flow is mechanically absent over my entire window. I considered this seriously and rejected it for two reasons. First, weekend ETF closure removes the BUYER as well as the seller, so it is close to symmetric; it is only net-positive by the size of the recent net flow, and $13.29M is noise. Second, 'the seller is on vacation' is the absence of a negative, not the presence of an edge, and it pairs with the lowest expected move on the board. ETH's bid, by contrast, is structural and does not switch off on a Saturday: more than 42 million ETH locked in staking, exchange balances down ~15% from early June to mid-August, and ETH spot ETFs leading the 2026 flow race at roughly +$863M net against about -$1B for BTC. A staking ETF pays ~2% yield on top of price exposure, which is the institutional story BTC structurally cannot match. That float-tightening runs continuously, and it is the reason ETH's 33.04% gain from 8/11 to 9/10 beat BTC's 22.96% -- the first time this year ETH has outperformed on the way UP rather than merely bounced harder. I would rather own a modest continuation in the asset with an actual supply mechanism than the flat asset with a paused seller. CHOSEN OVER, WITH THE COMPARATIVE ARGUMENT STATED: (a) SPOT BTC at 77,345.96 -- the runner-up, argued above; if I am wrong today it will most likely be because BTC's lower beta was worth more than ETH's momentum into a hike week, and I want that stated in advance. (b) SPOT SOL at 102.05 -- nearly identical 24h momentum to ETH (+2.78% vs +2.82%), so on the relative- strength screen alone it ties. Rejected because it is the higher-variance expression of the SAME trade with none of the structural support: no staking-ETF flow story, a far smaller float, and materially worse weekend liquidity. Taking more beta for the same signal is the opposite of what the mandate asks for. (c) SPOT XRP at 1.3718 (+0.65%) -- the single most direct CLARITY Act beneficiary, since the bill hands the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over digital commodity spot markets and resolves the classification question XRP has lived under for years. Rejected on timing and on character: the cloture vote is Tuesday, outside my window, and it is a binary political event requiring at least seven Democratic or independent votes on top of all 53 Republicans, which I have no ability to forecast. Positioning today for a Tuesday whip count is not a 24-hour trade. (d) SPOT LTC 54.18 (+0.85%), LINK 11.55 (+0.37%), DOGE 0.08498 (+0.73%), AVAX 7.442 (-0.07%), ADA 0.2087 -- all rejected as pure beta with no catalyst; AVAX is outright red on the day and would be a momentum trade against momentum. (e) ANY LEVERAGED WRAPPER -- BITX, the 2X Solana fund, SOXL/SOXS, the ORCL 2x products -- all unavailable, equity market closed. Noting explicitly that if today were a weekday the leverage question would be live and I would probably be sizing it; the constraint is the calendar, not a view. (f) 100% CASH -- the honest option on a genuinely low-edge day, and closer to being right than usual. Rejected because ETH offers a real, non-weekend-dependent structural bid and a confirmed relative-strength trend, which clears the bar for deploying; a book that must rotate daily should sit out only when it would otherwise be buying pure noise, and this is not pure noise. But I will note the margin is thin. ON THE LEVERAGE AND VARIANCE QUESTION, PRE-EMPTIVELY. Spot ETH at 1x will most likely produce a 1-4% move in either direction over a weekend session -- a modest outcome for a book whose stated purpose is asymmetric payoff, and the second consecutive day I have taken the low-variance route. Yesterday that choice was arguably timidity; today it is a binding constraint, since no leveraged instrument is tradable. What I want on the record is that I am NOT overcorrecting out of yesterday's loss. The ORCL error was not that I took risk -- it was that I took 100% event risk on a macro print I explicitly wrote that I could not forecast. Today there is no event inside the window, so the risk I am taking is ordinary directional risk in the asset with the best verifiable signal. That is a different decision, not a scared one.
positions.risks: THE PRIMARY RISK IS THAT RELATIVE STRENGTH IS THE WEAKEST CATEGORY OF SIGNAL I TRADE, AND IT IS ESSENTIALLY ALL I HAVE TODAY. 'ETH went up more than BTC yesterday, therefore it will go up more than BTC today' is momentum extrapolation over a single 24-hour observation, on a weekend, in thin books. It is not a catalyst and I should not dress it as one. The structural staking and ETF-flow argument is real but it operates on a timescale of months, not one session, so it justifies owning ETH over BTC in general far better than it justifies owning it specifically tonight. WEEKEND LIQUIDITY CUTS BOTH WAYS AND I AM ON THE HIGHER-BETA SIDE OF IT. Thin Saturday books amplify moves in either direction; ETH is the higher-beta asset of the two majors, so if anything hits the tape -- an exchange incident, a large liquidation cascade, a headline out of Washington ahead of Tuesday -- I take more of it than a BTC holder would. My 10% stop is again a number in a JSON file and not a resting order, which yesterday cost me real money when ORCL traded straight through 154.16. Crypto trades 24/7, so unlike an equity there is no gap mechanism -- but there is also no close, and a 3am move is fully live against me with nobody watching. THE MACRO IS A HEADWIND AND I AM LEANING INTO IT, NOT AWAY. A 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% is now 80-90% priced for Wednesday. ETH is a long-duration, zero-cashflow, maximally rate-sensitive asset -- the same characteristic that just destroyed my ORCL position. I am arguing the repricing is largely paid for and the event is outside my window, but that is the identical argument I made yesterday about CPI being 'pre-paid,' and yesterday it was wrong: the market found more room to reprice than I thought it had. I should hold that parallel in view rather than explain it away. Sunday-evening positioning into the Tuesday cloture vote could also cut either direction, and if the whip count starts leaking negative over the weekend, crypto beta sells off with ETH leading. COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM DISCOUNTING, STATED FAIRLY. BTC spot ETF outflows have run four straight sessions and roughly -$1B net for 2026 -- that is persistent institutional distribution across the whole complex, and ETH does not get a pass from it just because its own flow line is better. The research also notes ETH ETF inflows 'slowed sharply' recently while BTC took in $3.8B between 8/18 and 9/5, so the flow leadership I am citing is a year-to-date statistic that may already be rolling over; I am using a cumulative number to justify a one-day trade, which is a real weakness in the argument. And the 0.035 ETH/BTC level that the research says is required on a WEEKLY basis to confirm genuine rotation has not been reclaimed -- at 0.03275 I am buying a trend that is still unconfirmed by its own stated test. THE PROCESS LESSON FROM YESTERDAY, RECORDED PLAINLY. On 9/10 I fabricated an earnings reaction that had not occurred; I corrected it on 9/11 and then lost 9.88% on the position anyway, for reasons I had correctly written into my own risk section and did not act on. Naming a risk is not managing it. The specific correction going forward: when I write 'this is THE risk, not a background risk' about an event inside my holding window, that sentence should change the POSITION, not just the paragraph. Today it did -- the absence of any event inside the window is a load-bearing reason I am comfortable deploying at all. PRICING AND PROCEDURE, STATED PLAINLY.
